title: Your First Hello World App
description: Create an app called `greetings` and make it display 'Hello, Django!' at the URL `/greet/`.
problemStatement:
## Build Your First View

Extend the project you created in Task 1 (or start fresh if you prefer).

1. Inside your Django project, create an app named `greetings`.
2. In `greetings/views.py`, write a view function that returns an `HttpResponse` with the text `"Hello, Django!"`.
3. Create a `urls.py` file inside the `greetings` app and define a URL pattern that maps the empty route (`''`) to your view.
4. Include the app’s URLs in the project’s main `urls.py` so that the view is accessible at `/greet/`.
5. Run the server and visit `http://127.0.0.1:8000/greet/` to see your message.
hints: Don’t forget to add the app to `INSTALLED_APPS` in `settings.py`.
In the project’s main `urls.py`, use `path('greet/', include('greetings.urls'))`.
The `urls.py` inside the app should contain `path('', views.your_view_name)`.
Your view must return an `HttpResponse` object.
expectedOutput: When you visit `http://127.0.0.1:8000/greet/`, the browser displays: Hello, Django!
solutionCode:
# greetings/views.py
from django.http import HttpResponse

def hello(request):
    return HttpResponse("Hello, Django!")

# greetings/urls.py
from django.urls import path
from . import views

urlpatterns = [
    path('', views.hello, name='hello'),
]

# project/urls.py (main)
from django.contrib import admin
from django.urls import path, include

urlpatterns = [
    path('admin/', admin.site.urls),
    path('greet/', include('greetings.urls')),
]

# settings.py – add 'greetings' to INSTALLED_APPS
INSTALLED_APPS = [
    'django.contrib.admin',
    'django.contrib.auth',
    ...
    'greetings',
]
